# Testament of Benjamin — 12
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Cantabrigiensis) | **Section:** Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs

---

Benjamin is the last. The youngest. The one born as Rachel died. His testament closes the book — and it does so with a vision of resurrection and judgment that no other testament quite reaches.

**1** He was 125 years old when he kissed his sons and said:

**2** I am the old-age child — born to my parents the way Isaac was born to Abraham. My mother Rachel died in labor with me. I had no milk from her. Bilhah nursed me. Rachel had prayed and fasted for twelve years after Joseph was born before she conceived me. My father loved her so deeply he had prayed to see two sons from her.

**3** Let me tell you what happened when I went to Egypt and Joseph recognized me.

**4** He asked me: What did they tell our father when they sold me?

**5** I told him: They dipped your robe in a kid's blood and sent it home. They said: Look at this — is it your son's coat?

**6** Joseph said: That's what happened. And while they were stripping my coat from me, they gave me bread and said: Don't weep, Joseph. We'll sell you for gold, and your God will be with you.

**7** One of them — Reuben — had been in terrible regret ever since. Joseph saw his spirit and had compassion on him.

**8** Now sons: love the LORD God of heaven and earth. Keep his commandments. Follow the example of Joseph.

**9** Keep your mind aimed at what is good — because the person whose mind is right sees everything rightly. Fear God and love your neighbor. Even if Beliar's spirits come after you to afflict you, they won't have dominion over you — not if you fear God. Not the way they didn't have dominion over Joseph, no matter how many people tried to destroy him.

**10** Joseph asked our father to pray for his brothers — to ask God not to hold what they'd done against them. And when he did, Jacob cried out: My good child, you have overcome your father's heart.

**11** Then Jacob held Joseph and kissed him for two hours, and he spoke a prophecy over him: In you the heavenly prophecy about the Lamb of God is fulfilled — the Savior of the world. A blameless one delivered up for the lawless. A sinless one dying for the ungodly, in the blood of the covenant, for the salvation of all peoples and Israel, destroying Beliar and all his servants.

**12** Sons, do you see what happens to the good man at the end? Follow his compassion. Then you too will wear crowns of glory.

**13** The good person has no dark eye. He shows mercy even to those who sin against him, even to those who are plotting against him. Goodness overcomes evil. The beloved of God is loved by everyone.

**14** Flee from Beliar's malice. His sword has seven evils in it: bloodshed, ruin, tribulation, exile, famine, panic, desolation. That's what Cain got — seven vengeances from God, a new plague every hundred years until he was destroyed in the nine-hundredth year.

**15** So: do truth to one another. Keep the law. Give this as your inheritance to your children, as Abraham and Isaac and Jacob gave it to you: Keep the commands of God until the LORD reveals his salvation to all peoples.

**16** In that day you will see Enoch and Noah and Shem and Abraham and Isaac and Jacob — rising on the right hand, in gladness. And we will rise too, each one over our tribe, worshipping the King of heaven who appeared on earth in the form of a humble man. Those who believed in him on earth will rejoice with him. All the dead will rise — some to glory, some to shame.

**17** And the LORD will judge Israel first, because when he appeared as God in the flesh to rescue them, they did not believe him. Then he will judge all the nations who did not believe him. And he will use the faithful among the nations to convict Israel — the way he used Midianites against Esau.

**18** But if you walk in holiness, sons — if you keep his commands — you will dwell securely, and all Israel will be gathered to the LORD.

**19** And I will no longer be called a ravening wolf because of your violence. I will be called a worker of the LORD, distributing food to those who do good.

**20** In the last days there will arise one beloved of the LORD, from Judah and Levi — one who does God's will in his speech, who enlightens the nations with new knowledge. Until the end he will be in the gatherings of the nations, among their leaders, like a song on everyone's lips. His work and his words will be written in the holy books. He will be God's chosen one forever.

**21** Sons: obey the LORD. Flee Beliar's works.

**22** After he said this, Benjamin fell into a sweet sleep. In the morning his sons found that he had died. Thirty days later they carried him to Hebron and buried him with his fathers.

---
*End of Testament of Benjamin*
*End of the Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs*
